findings.passage: Today’s proposal would enshrine Wisconsin’s restrictive voter ID law into the state constitution, making it almost impossible for eligible voters whose rights are violated to seek redress in court.
findings.note: Press release in her name (posted by Urban Milwaukee, which carries no date on the page; the content concerns the Senate's voter ID constitutional amendment, which took place in January 2025). She describes the amendment as writing the voter ID law into the constitution and limiting court challenges.

findings.passage: But rather than tackle any of these important issues, Republican politicians are back to their tired playbook – cynical partisan power grabs to rig the system so they can keep power, this time by putting anti-voter measures in our state constitution.
findings.note: Same release. She calls the voter ID amendment an anti-voter measure and objects to putting it in the constitution.

findings.passage: In this next legislative session, we can and must come together to pass reasonable gun safety measures to reduce firearm injuries and deaths.
findings.note: Statement in her name after a school shooting in her district, saying she wants gun safety measures passed in the next session. Same statement also says guns are the number one cause of death for American children and that this is a policy choice.
subjects: general statement on gun safety laws

findings.passage: In the name of John Klang, Jonathan Brostoff, the victims of today’s shooting, and all those whose lives or loved ones have been lost to gun violence, we must choose to love our children more than we value unfettered access to guns.
findings.note: Closing line of her statement after the school shooting, setting children's safety against unrestricted access to guns.
subjects: general statement on gun safety laws

findings.passage: “This legislation aims to change that and bring Wisconsin into line with the other states who recognize that our colleges and universities are places for learning, for the free exchange of ideas, for deepening your knowledge and advancing your careers, and not for weapons,” Roys told the Wire.
